nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$, with numerical radius $w(T)$. For every $x \in H$, $|\operatorname{Im} \langle Tx, x\rangle| / \|x\|^2 \le w(T)$, where division by zero is taken to be $0$, so the case $x = 0$ is trivial.
nodes.title: Numerical radius bounds the normalized imaginary part of the quadratic form

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$, with numerical radius $w(T)$. For every $x \in H$, the Rayleigh quotient $R_T(x) = \operatorname{Re} \langle Tx, x\rangle / \|x\|^2$, taken to be $0$ at $x = 0$, satisfies $|R_T(x)| \le w(T)$.
nodes.title: Numerical radius bounds the Rayleigh quotient

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$, with numerical radius $w(T)$. For every $x \in H$, $|\operatorname{Re} \langle Tx, x\rangle| / \|x\|^2 \le w(T)$, where division by zero is taken to be $0$, so the case $x = 0$ is trivial.
nodes.title: Numerical radius bounds the normalized real part of the quadratic form

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$. The set $\{|\langle Tx, x\rangle| : x \in H,\ \|x\| = 1\}$ is bounded above.
nodes.title: The numerical-radius family is bounded above

nodes.summary: Every bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space satisfies $T = A + iB$, where $A = (T + T^*)/2$ and $B = (T - T^*)/(2i)$ are the real and imaginary Cartesian parts of $T$ and $T^*$ is the adjoint of $T$.
nodes.title: Cartesian decomposition

nodes.summary: For a bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space with adjoint $T^*$, the imaginary Cartesian part of $T$ is the bounded linear operator $(T - T^*)/(2i)$.
nodes.title: Imaginary Cartesian part of an operator

nodes.summary: For a bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space with adjoint $T^*$, the real Cartesian part of $T$ is the bounded linear operator $(T + T^*)/2$.
nodes.title: Real Cartesian part of an operator

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex Hilbert space $E$, whose inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is conjugate-linear in its first argument and linear in its second, and let $W(A) = \{\langle A x, x \rangle : x \in E,\ \|x\| = 1\}$ be the numerical range of $A$. If $z$ is in the spectrum of $A$, then the complex conjugate $\overline{z}$ lies in the closure of $W(A)$.
nodes.title: Conjugates of spectral values lie in the closed numerical range

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $E$, whose inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is conjugate-linear in its first argument and linear in its second, let $W(A) = \{\langle A x, x \rangle : x \in E,\ \|x\| = 1\}$ be the numerical range of $A$ and let $z \in \mathbb{C}$. If there is a vector $x \in E$ with $\|x\| = 1$ and $A x = z x$, then the complex conjugate…
nodes.title: Conjugates of eigenvalues lie in the numerical range

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$, conjugate-linear in the first argument and linear in the second, and let $T : H \to H$ be a bounded linear operator. Let $N(T) = \{\langle \psi, T\psi \rangle : \psi \in H,\ \|\psi\| = 1\} \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be the numerical range of $T$, and for $z \in \mathbb{C}$ let $d(z, N(T))$ be the infimum of the distances from $z$ to…
nodes.title: Lower bound from the numerical range

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $E$. For every $x \in E$ with $\|x\| = 1$, the number $\langle A x, x \rangle$ lies in the numerical range $W(A)$.
nodes.title: Unit vectors give points of the numerical range

nodes.summary: For every bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space $H$ with adjoint $T^*$, the imaginary Cartesian part $B = (T - T^*)/(2i)$ is symmetric: $\langle Bx, y\rangle = \langle x, By\rangle$ for all $x, y \in H$.
nodes.title: The imaginary Cartesian part is symmetric

nodes.summary: For every bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space $H$ with adjoint $T^*$, the real Cartesian part $A = (T + T^*)/2$ is symmetric: $\langle Ax, y\rangle = \langle x, Ay\rangle$ for all $x, y \in H$.
nodes.title: The real Cartesian part is symmetric

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex Hilbert space $E$, whose inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is conjugate-linear in its first argument and linear in its second, let $W(A) = \{\langle A x, x \rangle : x \in E,\ \|x\| = 1\}$ be the numerical range of $A$ and let $\mu \in \mathbb{C}$. If $\mu$ is not in the closure of $W(A)$, then $A - \overline{\mu}\, I$, where $\overline{\mu}$ is the…
nodes.title: Conjugate shifts off the closed numerical range are invertible

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$, with numerical radius $w(T)$. For every $x \in H$ with $\|x\| = 1$, $|\langle Tx, x\rangle| \le w(T)$.
nodes.title: The numerical radius bounds the quadratic form on unit vectors

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $E$. A complex number $c$ lies in the numerical range $W(A)$ if and only if there is a vector $x \in E$ with $\|x\| = 1$ and $\langle A x, x \rangle = c$.
nodes.title: Membership in the numerical range

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space, with adjoint $T^*$, and let $B = (T - T^*)/(2i)$ be its imaginary Cartesian part. Then $\|B\| \le w(T)$, where $\|B\|$ is the operator norm of $B$ and $w(T)$ is the numerical radius of $T$.
nodes.title: Norm of the imaginary part is at most the numerical radius

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space, with adjoint $T^*$, and let $A = (T + T^*)/2$ be its real Cartesian part. Then $\|A\| \le w(T)$, where $\|A\|$ is the operator norm of $A$ and $w(T)$ is the numerical radius of $T$.
nodes.title: Norm of the real part is at most the numerical radius

nodes.summary: For every bounded operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space, $\|T\| \le 2\,w(T)$, where $\|T\|$ is the operator norm and $w(T)$ is the numerical radius of $T$.
nodes.title: Operator norm at most twice the numerical radius

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a nonzero vector in a complex inner product space. Then the vector $\|x\|^{-1} x$ has norm $1$.
nodes.title: Normalizing a nonzero vector gives a unit vector

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$, with adjoint $T^*$. For every $x \in H$, $|\langle T^* x, x\rangle| = |\langle T x, x\rangle|$, since $\langle T^* x, x\rangle$ is the complex conjugate of $\langle T x, x\rangle$.
nodes.title: The quadratic form of the adjoint has the same modulus

nodes.summary: For every bounded operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space, the numerical radius of its adjoint $T^*$ equals the numerical radius of $T$: $w(T^*) = w(T)$.
nodes.title: Numerical radius of the adjoint

nodes.summary: If $T$ is a self-adjoint bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space, then its numerical radius equals its operator norm: $w(T) = \|T\|$.
nodes.title: Numerical radius of a self-adjoint operator

nodes.summary: For every bounded operator $T$ on a complex inner product space, the numerical radius $w(T)$ is at most the operator norm: $w(T) \le \|T\|$.
nodes.title: Numerical radius at most the operator norm

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex inner product space $H$ and let $c \ge 0$ be a real number. If $|\langle T x, x\rangle| \le c$ for every unit vector $x \in H$, then the numerical radius of $T$ satisfies $w(T) \le c$.
nodes.title: Bounding the numerical radius from above

nodes.summary: For every bounded operator $T$ on a complex inner product space, the numerical radius $w(T)$ of $T$ satisfies $w(T) \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the numerical radius

nodes.summary: The numerical radius of a bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space $H$ is the real number $w(T) = \sup \{ |\langle T x, x \rangle| : x \in H,\ \|x\| = 1 \}$, the supremum of the moduli of the values $\langle T x, x \rangle$ over the unit vectors of $H$ (taken to be $0$ when $H = 0$).
nodes.title: Numerical radius

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $E$. Then every point of the numerical range $W(A)$ has absolute value at most the operator norm $\|A\|$: $W(A)$ lies in the closed disc of radius $\|A\|$ centred at $0$.
nodes.title: The numerical range is bounded by the operator norm

nodes.summary: For a bounded linear operator $A$ on a complex inner product space $E$, the numerical range of $A$ is the set $W(A) = \{\langle A x, x \rangle : x \in E,\ \|x\| = 1\} \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, where the inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ of $E$ is conjugate-linear in its first argument and linear in its second.
nodes.title: Numerical range

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$, whose inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is conjugate-linear in its first argument, and let $B = (T - T^*)/(2i)$ be the imaginary Cartesian part of $T$. Then for every $x \in H$ one has $\langle B x, x \rangle = -\operatorname{Im} \langle T x, x \rangle$.
nodes.title: Quadratic form of the imaginary Cartesian part

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$ and let $A = (T + T^*)/2$ be the real Cartesian part of $T$. Then for every $x \in H$ one has $\langle A x, x \rangle = \operatorname{Re} \langle T x, x \rangle$.
nodes.title: Quadratic form of the real Cartesian part

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex inner product space $H$. For every $x \in H$, $\langle T(\|x\|^{-1} x), \|x\|^{-1} x \rangle = \|x\|^{-2} \langle T x, x \rangle$, where $0^{-1}$ is read as $0$, so that for $x = 0$ both sides vanish.
nodes.title: Quadratic form at the normalized vector

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex Hilbert space $E$, whose inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is conjugate-linear in its first argument and linear in its second, and let $W(A) = \{\langle A x, x \rangle : x \in E,\ \|x\| = 1\}$ be the numerical range of $A$. Then every point of the spectrum of $A$ is the complex conjugate $\overline{w}$ of some point $w$ of the closure of $W(A)$.
nodes.title: The spectrum lies in the conjugate of the closed numerical range

nodes.summary: The complex conjugate of $1/2 \in \mathbb{C}$ is $1/2$, that is, $\overline{1/2} = 1/2$.
nodes.title: Complex conjugate of one half

nodes.summary: The complex conjugate of $-i/2 \in \mathbb{C}$ is $i/2$, that is, $\overline{-i/2} = i/2$.
nodes.title: Complex conjugate of minus half the imaginary unit

nodes.summary: The numerical range of a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space is convex. Completeness of the space is not needed.
nodes.title: Toeplitz–Hausdorff theorem without completeness

nodes.summary: The numerical range of a bounded linear operator on a complex Hilbert space is convex.
nodes.title: Toeplitz–Hausdorff theorem
Analysis

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
